title: Motive and reciprocal inducement
summary: A party’s personal reason for contracting can differ from the performance or promise that serves as the agreed exchange.
notes:
Someone may paint for money while also seeking reputation, enjoyment, or friendship. Those additional motives do not remove the money from the bargain. The readings ask whether the promise and the requested return were given in exchange for each other; they do not require the exchange to be either party’s only motive. This distinction also prevents every beneficial consequence of a promise from being treated as consideration.

The text’s discussion of Restatement § 81 and Holmes’s reciprocal inducement formulation distinguishes why a party desires an outcome from the act requested as its price. A promise made partly from affection may remain bargained for. Conversely, reliance or a benefit occurring without being sought in exchange does not become consideration merely because it helps explain the transaction.
